name: Typer workflow evaluation
notes: Workflow-oriented questions validated against the checked-out Typer repository.

questions.question: Which code converts a normal Python function into a CLI command?
important_facts: get_command_from_info builds a TyperCommand from callback and parameter metadata.

questions.question: How does Typer inspect a function signature?
important_facts: Typer inspects function parameters and derives parameter metadata and converters.

questions.question: Which module handles shell auto-completion?
important_facts: typer/completion.py contains the public completion integration.

questions.question: Where is the help text for commands produced?
important_facts: Core command classes dispatch help formatting and rich_utils renders rich help.

questions.question: How does Typer decide whether a CLI parameter is required?
important_facts: Parameter metadata and defaults determine requiredness before TyperArgument is constructed.

questions.question: Which code is responsible for registering new commands?
important_facts: Typer.command is the command registration decorator.

questions.question: How are decorators translated into executable commands?
important_facts: The decorator stores CommandInfo and get_command_from_info turns it into a command object.

questions.question: Where are command-line flags represented?
important_facts: TyperOption represents runtime Click option behavior.

questions.question: Which class represents positional CLI arguments?
important_facts: TyperArgument represents positional arguments at runtime.

questions.question: How does Typer communicate with Click internally?
important_facts: Typer converts its metadata into Click-compatible command and group objects.

questions.question: How does Typer create a CLI application?
important_facts: Typer is the application object and run is a convenience entry point.

questions.question: Explain the lifecycle of a Typer command.
important_facts: Registration metadata is converted into an executable TyperCommand.

questions.question: How does Typer parse command-line arguments?
important_facts: Typer converts function parameters to Click parameters; Click performs runtime parsing.

questions.question: How are default values processed?
important_facts: Defaults pass from function inspection through metadata and Click parameter construction.

questions.question: How does Typer determine whether a parameter is an option or an argument?
important_facts: ParameterInfo type determines whether get_click_param constructs a TyperOption or TyperArgument.

questions.question: How are type annotations converted into Click parameter types?
important_facts: Annotation metadata is inspected and mapped to Click parameter types.

questions.question: Which modules are involved when a command is executed?
important_facts: main builds commands, models stores metadata, and core provides executable Click-compatible classes.

questions.question: How are callbacks executed?
important_facts: Typer.callback registers callback metadata and get_callback wraps execution and conversion.

questions.question: How does Typer build Click commands from Python functions?
important_facts: Function parameters and CommandInfo are converted into a TyperCommand.

questions.question: Explain the command registration pipeline.
important_facts: The decorator records command information and command construction later produces executable Click objects.
